This is so completely absurd. Copyright law is so horribly outdated and out of touch. This is one of the things that Aaron Swartz actively fought against (not this particular case, but old, BAD copyright law). In fact, he was arrested for downloading documents from JSTOR in bulk from MIT's servers, which he was doing because they had complete copyright control over a huge amount of academic knowledge (and profit quite handsomely from it might I add).

Good article. I really hope something positive comes out of this, but it seems that nothing will change until there is a massive public outcry

They say that modifying games to connect to a new server (or to avoid contacting a server at all) after publisher support ends—letting people continue to play the games they paid for—will destroy the video game industry. They say it would “undermine the fundamental copyright principles on which our copyright laws are based.”

...how?

A good example of abandonware preservation is the game Freelancer. Long since forgotten by Microsoft it's still played regularly and continues to be modded entirely by the community that enjoys it. It harms no one.
Simultaneously funny and infuriating. Like they think just because they don't want us to make the games we paid for playable, that we won't do it anyway? Pfff. Riiiiight.
I say do what you want with so called abandoned games. Who is going to do anything about it?

Museums and Archives should be exempt from this kind of stuff. Just entirely. In another 30 years we'll look back on the beginning of our medium and find nothing, and that'll be a sad day, rather like how film looks back to silent movies and how many of them were lost or destroyed.

Our past should be protected from future greed. Fuck copyright and all of it's nonsense when it comes to Museums or Archives, make the laws better if they conflict, otherwise we'll have no heritage in the future.
